questions.q: What are the three architectural components centralized governance needs, per this lesson?
options: A single enterprise metadata hub, a single policy engine, and a single access-provisioning queue
A central index plus fully autonomous domain catalogs
No metadata layer is needed at all
Multiple independent catalogs with no coordination
questions.explain: The lesson names three required components: one metadata hub, one policy engine, one access-provisioning queue.

questions.q: Why does centralized architecture avoid the problem of 'drift' between definitions?
options: There's only one copy of the policy and schema, so there's nowhere for drift to come from
Drift is prevented by a separate dedicated anti-drift team
Drift only happens in federated architectures, never centralized ones by definition
Centralized architectures automatically detect and fix drift using AI
questions.explain: The lesson states there's no drift to reconcile because there's only one copy of policy, schema, and process.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what causes the centralized model's bottleneck?
options: Bottlenecks only occur if the company is using outdated software
The central team is inherently slow or badly managed
Every request has to pass through the same single hub, policy engine, and provisioning queue, with no way to parallelize
Centralized architectures have no policy engine at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates the bottleneck from team competence — it's structural: no mechanism to parallelize across domains.

questions.q: What scaling levers does the lesson say can push a centralized architecture's bottleneck further out, without changing the model?
options: Hiring unlimited additional central staff with no automation
Self-service connectors, automated classification, and workflow automation for routine access requests
Removing the policy engine entirely
Switching immediately to a full data mesh
questions.explain: The lesson lists automation levers (self-service onboarding, automated classification, workflow rules) that scale centralized architecture without changing its model.

questions.q: Which reference-architecture pattern from Lesson 3 does centralized governance apply directly, per this lesson?
options: No reference-architecture pattern applies to centralized governance
Catalog-of-catalogs, with a lightweight index only
Hub-and-spoke, with the hub holding full detail rather than just an index
Mesh of catalogs, with no central system
questions.explain: The lesson states centralized governance applies hub-and-spoke directly, with the hub holding the full detail, not just an index.
